paper.title: Common Authentication Threats
paper.context: Review redacted evidence from fictional systems. Keep observed facts, hypotheses, containment and verification distinct.

objectives.read-auth-signals: Distinguish focused guessing, suspected reuse and confirmed credential exposure.
objectives.trace-session-transition: Verify that sign-in establishes a fresh session identity and logout invalidates it.
objectives.audit-observation: Preserve diagnostic value without exposing account existence or credential material.
objectives.test-containment: Separate age, withdrawal and proof requirements in the serving decision.
objectives.verify-auth-contract: Verify a complete authentication boundary before reopening a protected route.

questions.prompt: An incident owner confirms a workload credential was included in an exported support artifact. What should the service owner do first?

choices.alpha: Wait for evidence of unauthorized access
choices.beta: Restrict the artifact and withdraw the exposed credential
choices.gamma: Search all logs for the raw credential and send its matches to chat
choices.delta: Require a password change for every employee

questions.prompt: A team wants to reduce the effect of a password breach at an unrelated service. Which change addresses password reuse directly?

choices.beta: Raise the maximum password length only
choices.gamma: Support a password manager and unique passwords, with breached-password screening

questions.prompt: One account shows a rapidly rising count of failed sign-ins and no success. What is the best immediate interpretation?

choices.alpha: Focused guessing is plausible and merits checking account-aware throttling
choices.beta: The displayed name is necessarily a real account

questions.prompt: A service sees MFA challenges after unusual password successes across unrelated accounts. What is the sound next step?

choices.alpha: Treat each password success as proof of full authentication
choices.beta: Infer a specific source breach from the aggregate alone
choices.gamma: Disable MFA to see whether the successes continue
choices.delta: Investigate possible credential reuse with redacted evidence and preserve the MFA gate

questions.prompt: A token was copied into monitoring data. The gateway stopped recording the field. What additional concern remains?

choices.alpha: The change rewrites historical telemetry automatically
choices.beta: Older copies may remain and the presented bearer evidence may still be accepted
choices.gamma: TLS makes copies in storage unreadable
choices.delta: A readable token proves its signing key is compromised

questions.prompt: An API requires proof tied to the client’s certificate. A valid bearer-style credential alone reaches the API under the stated design. What should happen?

choices.alpha: Withhold protected data until the required bound proof is verified
choices.beta: Grant access because the credential was recently issued
choices.gamma: Grant access if the token’s text matches a known format

questions.prompt: A regression suite tests the protection at successful sign-in. Which assertion directly checks the session-identity transition?

choices.alpha: The browser has an HttpOnly cookie before sign-in
choices.beta: The response body contains a welcome message
choices.gamma: The authenticated reference differs and the old reference cannot restore the authenticated state
choices.delta: The server logs the old reference

questions.prompt: The service owner confirms an already authenticated browser reference was exposed. What specifically cuts off that reference at the server?

choices.alpha: Set HttpOnly on newly issued cookies
choices.beta: Delete the cookie from one browser
choices.gamma: Change the public login error message
choices.delta: Invalidate the affected server session and verify the reference no longer restores identity

questions.prompt: Two login failures have identical JSON and status, but unknown accounts return much faster than wrong evidence. What is the review finding?

choices.alpha: Enumeration risk can remain because timing is observable
choices.beta: The public contract is secure because the text matches
choices.gamma: The app should document the account status in a public header
choices.delta: Neither timing nor body matters under HTTPS

questions.prompt: A team needs to investigate sign-in failures across a gateway and API. Which event shape best balances diagnosis and confidentiality?

choices.alpha: Full headers and an encrypted file attachment
choices.beta: Correlation ID, timestamp, failure category and controlled access
choices.gamma: The session cookie with a visible account name
choices.delta: A screenshot of each failed form submission

questions.prompt: Read the Java fixture. The current state is available and unrevoked, but now.equals(expiry) is true. What follows?

choices.alpha: Accept because the state is current
choices.beta: Accept if the second factor was verified
choices.gamma: Refuse because equal instants do not satisfy isBefore
choices.delta: Refuse only because one nanosecond must be added to now

questions.prompt: Write a reopening checklist after an internal review finds that a protected export can see a principal before a required factor completes and that revoked sessions sometimes keep working. Include public responses, internal evidence, and positive and negative tests.

feedback.alpha: Confirmed exposure is enough to start containment.
feedback.beta: Removing access to the artifact limits further spread, and withdrawal removes the credential’s accepted status on supporting paths.
feedback.gamma: That spreads secret material into additional systems.
feedback.delta: The affected evidence identifies a workload.

exposure-triage.reason: Contain the exposure using the affected identifier and sanitized evidence.

feedback.beta: Allowing longer choices does not prevent repeated choices.
feedback.gamma: Unique choices separate the services, and screening reduces acceptance of compromised choices.
feedback.delta: The affected control is the user’s password.

unique-passwords.reason: Reduce reuse and complement it with phishing-resistant authentication.

feedback.alpha: The concentration supports this hypothesis without proving credential theft.
feedback.beta: A submitted identifier is not verified existence.
feedback.delta: The origin of the evidence is unknown.

focused-pattern.reason: Compare failure concentration with baseline and apply bounded defensive controls.

feedback.alpha: A later factor still gates full authentication.
feedback.beta: The aggregate does not identify the source.
feedback.gamma: That removes a defensive gate during investigation.
feedback.delta: Distributed anomalies justify investigation, while MFA still protects the serving boundary.

distributed-review.reason: Compare events across accounts without collecting raw credentials.

feedback.alpha: Stored data and downstream copies have separate retention.
feedback.beta: Contain archives and withdraw the credential where verification can observe it.
feedback.gamma: Transport protection ends at the connection boundary.
feedback.delta: Disclosure of a token does not prove loss of the private key.

leak-scope.reason: Verify redaction at collection, storage and export boundaries.

feedback.alpha: An accepted token does not substitute for the associated possession proof.
feedback.beta: Freshness alone does not establish possession proof.
feedback.delta: The verifier must check the relationship specified by the credential profile.

bound-proof.reason: Test that required proof is both valid and tied to the expected evidence.

feedback.alpha: Cookie accessibility does not confirm rotation.
feedback.beta: UI output does not prove session behavior.
feedback.gamma: The privilege transition must break the old reference’s association.
feedback.delta: Logging secrets worsens exposure and does not validate rotation.

transition-check.reason: Check accepted state through the server, including the prior reference boundary.

feedback.alpha: That limits script access, but does not withdraw a current server-side record.
feedback.beta: Other holders can still present the reference until the server rejects it.
feedback.delta: The server rejects subsequent use once its authoritative state reflects invalidation.

contain-session.reason: Test server-side invalidation independently from browser cleanup.

feedback.alpha: Observable timing differences can disclose state.
feedback.beta: Text is only one public signal.
feedback.gamma: That would disclose the information directly.
feedback.delta: The requesting client still sees the response and timing.

observable-negative.reason: Compare the full externally visible behavior across negative paths.

feedback.alpha: Storing complete credentials is unnecessary for this investigation.
feedback.beta: These fields correlate incidents without retaining evidence content.
feedback.gamma: The session reference is itself sensitive evidence.
feedback.delta: Form data can include passwords and unnecessary personal information.

telemetry-shape.reason: Use a stable correlation identifier and an allowlisted schema.

feedback.alpha: Current state is only one required condition.
feedback.beta: An earlier verification does not extend the declared boundary.
feedback.gamma: The deadline is exclusive even when authority state is current.
feedback.delta: No adjustment is needed to evaluate equality.

deadline-and-state.reason: Test one instant before, exactly at, and just after the cutoff.

reopen-contract.reason: Keep the principal unauthenticated while a required factor is pending or rejected. Verify full completion, rotate the reference on the transition and require current valid session state. Make the serving path observe invalidation and withhold protected data when required state is unavailable. Authorize the verified principal for exports separately. Preserve generic public failures and allowlisted internal events. Exercise pending, rejected, verified, invalidated, unavailable and exact-expiry cases with redacted evidence.
rubric: Gate principal establishment on all required factors.
Explain server-side invalidation and unavailable-state behavior.
Keep authentication, authorization and expiry checks distinct.
Specify consistent public feedback and redacted internal correlation.
Include positive, negative and exact-boundary checks.
